Yes, Kenya produces medicine, boasting the largest pharmaceutical manufacturing sector in East Africa. However, the country still imports roughly 70% to 80% of its total pharmaceutical products—mostly from India and China. [](https://theconversation.com/how-kenyan-and-tanzanian-medicine-producers-deserve-a-shot-in-the-arm-65578)

- **Market share:** Domestic factories supply about 20% to 30% of the country's total medicine needs. [](https://trial.medpath.com/news/kenya-launches-five-year-local-manufacturing-strategy-to-reduce-pharmaceutical-import-dependence)

- **Capabilities:** Local plants produce basic essential formulations including tablets, capsules, syrups, creams, ointments, and intravenous (IV) fluids. [](https://theconversation.com/how-kenyan-and-tanzanian-medicine-producers-deserve-a-shot-in-the-arm-65578)

- **Strategy:** Kenya launched the _Health Products and Technologies Local Manufacturing Strategy (2026–2030)_ to scale up domestic manufacturing and reduce heavy import reliance. [](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q5ZO9yidM04)

### Key Local Manufacturers

- **Cosmos Limited:** A major Nairobi-based regional producer of generic human medicines.

- **Universal Corporation Ltd (UCL):** Located near Nairobi, it manufactures over 100 formulations.

- **Dawa Pharmaceuticals / Dawa Life Sciences:** Produces a wide range of essential pharmaceutical products.

- **Beta Healthcare:** Manufactures common over-the-counter and prescription drugs. [](https://theconversation.com/how-kenyan-and-tanzanian-medicine-producers-deserve-a-shot-in-the-arm-65578)
